questions.title: Longest substring without repeating characters
questions.prompt:
Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.

Example: s = "abcabcbb" → 3 ("abc")

Discuss your approach, then write the code.

questions.title: Thread-safe bounded queue
questions.prompt:
Implement a thread-safe bounded blocking queue in Java (or Python) with put() and get() methods.

Discuss the synchronization strategy, potential deadlocks, and how you'd test it.

questions.title: Binary search and its variants
questions.prompt:
Implement binary search on a sorted array. Then extend it to find the first and last position of a target value.

Analyze the time and space complexity and discuss edge cases.

questions.title: Lowest common ancestor of a binary tree
questions.prompt:
Given a binary tree and two nodes p and q, find their lowest common ancestor.

Solve it for: (a) a general binary tree, (b) a binary search tree. What changes between the two?

questions.title: Coin change problem
questions.prompt:
Given coin denominations and a target amount, find the minimum number of coins to make the amount.

Discuss the greedy approach and why it fails, then implement the dynamic programming solution.

questions.title: Connected components and cycle detection
questions.prompt:
Implement BFS and DFS on an adjacency list. Use one to find all connected components and the other to detect a cycle in an undirected graph.

Discuss trade-offs between BFS and DFS.

questions.title: Merge overlapping intervals
questions.prompt:
Given a list of intervals [start, end], merge all overlapping ones and return the result.

Example: [[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]] → [[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]]

What is the time complexity? How would you handle a streaming input?

questions.title: Fast power function with overflow handling
questions.prompt:
Implement pow(x, n) (x raised to the power n) efficiently, handling negative exponents and potential integer overflow.

Explain the divide-and-conquer approach and its time complexity versus the naive loop.

questions.title: Design a payment processing system
questions.prompt:
Design a payment processing system that handles 10,000 transactions per second.

Requirements:
- Idempotent payment submission
- At-least-once delivery with deduplication
- Real-time balance checks
- Audit trail for every state change

Walk through your high-level architecture, data model, and the trickiest consistency challenges.

questions.title: Design a distributed rate limiter
questions.prompt:
Design a distributed rate limiter that enforces per-user request limits across a fleet of API servers.

Consider: token bucket vs sliding window, Redis vs in-process, accuracy vs latency tradeoffs.

questions.title: CAP theorem and consistency trade-offs
questions.prompt:
A client wants strong consistency across all nodes in their distributed database. Explain the CAP theorem and why this is impossible under network partitions.

Compare eventual consistency vs linearizability. Which real-world systems choose which, and why?

questions.title: Design an event-driven notification system
questions.prompt:
Design a notification system that delivers email, SMS, and push notifications triggered by user events (order placed, payment received, etc.).

Address: fan-out at scale, at-least-once vs exactly-once delivery, retry and dead-letter queues.

questions.title: Design a URL shortener
questions.prompt:
Design a URL shortening service (like bit.ly) that handles 100M URLs and 1B redirects per day.

Address: ID generation (no collisions), redirect latency, analytics, and storage choices.

questions.title: Distributed leader election and consensus
questions.prompt: Explain how Raft achieves consensus in a distributed system. Walk through a leader election scenario and a log replication scenario, including what happens when the leader fails mid-replication.

questions.title: Design a full-text search system
questions.prompt:
Design a full-text search system for a document corpus of 1 billion documents.

Address: inverted index construction, tokenization and stemming, ranking (TF-IDF or BM25), and how you'd handle real-time index updates.

questions.title: Design a distributed cache
questions.prompt:
Design a distributed in-memory cache (similar to Redis Cluster) that supports GET, SET, and TTL.

Address: consistent hashing for key distribution, replication for availability, eviction policies (LRU/LFU), and cold-start/cache-warming strategies.

questions.title: Disagreement with a technical decision
questions.prompt:
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a technical decision made by your team or manager.

What was the decision? How did you handle the disagreement? What was the outcome?

questions.title: Taking ownership of a hard problem
questions.prompt:
Describe a situation where you took ownership of a complex, ambiguous problem that wasn't originally yours to solve.

What made it complex? What did you do? What was the result?

questions.title: Mentoring a junior engineer
questions.prompt:
Tell me about a time you mentored or coached a junior engineer.

What was their struggle? What approach did you take? How did you measure success?

questions.title: Learning from a production incident
questions.prompt:
Describe a production incident you were involved in — either caused by your code or one you helped resolve.

What happened? What was your role? What did you change afterward to prevent recurrence?

questions.title: Managing competing deadlines
questions.prompt:
Tell me about a time when you had multiple high-priority tasks competing for your attention.

How did you prioritize? What trade-offs did you make? What would you do differently?

questions.title: Cross-team collaboration challenge
questions.prompt:
Describe a project that required working closely with a team outside your own (product, ops, data, another engineering team).

What made it difficult? How did you build alignment? What was the outcome?

questions.title: Working with unclear requirements
questions.prompt:
Tell me about a project where the requirements were vague or frequently changing.

How did you approach the ambiguity? How did you decide when to ask for clarity vs move forward? What was the result?

questions.title: Biggest technical growth moment
questions.prompt:
What is the most significant technical concept or skill you have taught yourself in the last two years?

What drove you to learn it? How did you approach the learning? How has it changed your work?
